cards.definition: A sequence f_n converges pointwise to f on X if for every x in X and epsilon>0 there is N=N(x,epsilon) such that n≥N implies |f_n(x)-f(x)|<epsilon. Dependence on x is permitted, not required. A single N working for all x proves the stronger property of uniform convergence and is also a valid proof of pointwise convergence.
required_concepts: For each fixed x and epsilon, one index controls all later n.
N may depend on x.
A uniform bound is stronger but must still be accepted as proving pointwise convergence.
major_error_concepts: To show pointwise convergence, for each n one may choose a convenient x_n and check only f_n(x_n).

cards.prompt: What is Polynomial approximation theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It makes polynomials uniformly dense in continuous functions on a compact interval, justifying approximation by algebraic models; it is an existence theorem and does not supply the best degree, coefficients, or approximation rate by itself.
required_concepts: It makes polynomials uniformly dense in continuous functions on a compact interval, justifying approximation by algebraic models
it is an existence theorem and does not supply the best degree, coefficients, or approximation rate by itself.
major_error_concepts: Calling one Taylor polynomial a uniform approximation theorem for every continuous function.

cards.prompt: State Polynomial approximation theorem, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** The Weierstrass conclusion that continuous real functions on a compact interval can be uniformly approximated by polynomials with proof route and scope explicit.
required_concepts: The Weierstrass conclusion that continuous real functions on a compact interval can be uniformly approximated by polynomials with proof route
and scope explicit.
major_error_concepts: Calling one Taylor polynomial a uniform approximation theorem for every continuous function.

cards.prompt: Define Power-series termwise operations. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The theorem that inside the radius of convergence a power series is continuous and may be integrated and differentiated termwise with the derived series sharing the radius.
required_concepts: The theorem that inside the radius of convergence a power series is continuous
and may be integrated and differentiated termwise with the derived series sharing the radius.
major_error_concepts: Including endpoints without separate convergence checks.

cards.prompt: Define Supremum norm on bounded functions. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The supremum over the domain of the absolute function value whose induced metric makes uniform convergence exactly norm convergence.
required_concepts: The supremum over the domain of the absolute function value whose induced metric makes uniform convergence exactly norm convergence.
major_error_concepts: Using the maximum when the supremum is not attained.

cards.term: Termwise Riemann integration under uniform convergence
cards.prompt: Define Termwise Riemann integration under uniform convergence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: If each f_n is Riemann integrable on a fixed finite interval [a,b] and f_n→f uniformly there, then f is Riemann integrable and integral_a^b f_n→integral_a^b f. Indeed the integral error is at most (b-a) sup_{x in [a,b]}|f_n(x)-f(x)|. The finite-domain factor is essential; uniform convergence on an unbounded interval needs additional tail control.
required_concepts: Use one fixed finite interval and Riemann-integrable f_n.
Require uniform convergence.
The limit is integrable and the integral error is bounded by interval length times sup error.
major_error_concepts: Uniform convergence on [0,infinity) always permits exchanging the limit and improper integral without tail assumptions.

cards.prompt: Define Uniform Cauchy criterion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The criterion that for every epsilon all sufficiently late functions are uniformly close at every domain point with completeness of codomain needed for the converse.
required_concepts: First material clause: The criterion that for every epsilon all sufficiently late functions are uniformly
Remaining material clause: close at every domain point with completeness of codomain needed for the converse.
major_error_concepts: Assuming a limit exists in an incomplete codomain.

cards.term: Uniform convergence of a function series
cards.prompt: Define Uniform convergence of a function series. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The convergence of its partial-sum functions uniformly with absolute uniform convergence distinguished from conditional uniform behavior.
required_concepts: The convergence of its partial-sum functions uniformly with absolute uniform convergence distinguished from conditional uniform behavior.
major_error_concepts: Calling pointwise absolute convergence uniform absolute convergence.

cards.prompt: Define Uniform convergence of functions. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The quantifier order where for every epsilon one N works for all domain points equivalently the sup error tends to zero when finite.
required_concepts: The quantifier order where for every epsilon one N works for all domain points equivalently the sup error tends to zero when finite.
major_error_concepts: Checking finitely many x values.

cards.prompt: Define Uniform limit of continuous functions. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The theorem that a uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous proved by a three-term epsilon estimate.
required_concepts: The theorem that a uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous proved by a three-term epsilon estimate.
major_error_concepts: Replacing uniform convergence with pointwise convergence.

cards.prompt: Define Weierstrass M-test. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The theorem that uniform absolute bounds on each f_n by M_n with sum M_n convergent imply uniform absolute convergence of the function series.
required_concepts: The theorem that uniform absolute bounds on each f_n by M_n with sum M_n convergent imply uniform absolute convergence of the function series.
major_error_concepts: Choosing M_n depending on x.

cards.prompt: Define Absolute continuity preview. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The epsilon-delta control of sums of function increments over disjoint intervals and its stronger relation to the fundamental theorem than uniform continuity.
required_concepts: The epsilon-delta control of sums of function increments over disjoint intervals and its stronger relation to the fundamental theorem than uniform continuity.
major_error_concepts: Equating absolute continuity with uniform continuity.

cards.prompt: Define Baire-category preview. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The complete-metric-space theorem that a countable intersection of dense open sets is dense and its distinction from measure size.
required_concepts: The complete-metric-space theorem that a countable intersection of dense open sets is dense and its distinction from measure size.
major_error_concepts: Calling meagre equivalent to measure zero.

cards.prompt: What is Banach fixed-point theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It turns a contraction on a complete metric space into a unique fixed point and a convergent iteration with quantitative error control, supporting existence and algorithms simultaneously; a merely continuous or noncontractive map does not receive the guarantee.
required_concepts: It turns a contraction on a complete metric space into a unique fixed point and a convergent iteration with quantitative error control, supporting existence and algorithms simultaneously
a merely continuous or noncontractive map does not receive the guarantee.
major_error_concepts: Dropping completeness or the self-map condition.

cards.prompt: State the Banach fixed-point theorem with its space, self-map, uniform-factor, and convergence hypotheses.
cards.definition: Let T:X→X be a contraction with one factor 0≤q<1 on a nonempty complete metric space. Then T has a unique fixed point x*, and for every x_0 in X, x_(n+1)=T(x_n) converges to x*. In particular d(x_n,x*)≤q^n d(x_0,x*) for n≥1. Completeness, the self-map condition, and a uniform factor cannot simply be omitted.
required_concepts: The metric space is nonempty and complete.
T is a self-map with one contraction factor q<1.
There is a unique fixed point and every starting point converges geometrically.
major_error_concepts: On X=(0,1), T(x)=x/2 has a fixed point in X because it is a contraction, despite X not being complete.

cards.prompt: Define Cantor-function pathology. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The continuous nondecreasing function constant on removed intervals whose derivative is zero where defined off the Cantor set yet whose total rise is one.
required_concepts: The continuous nondecreasing function constant on removed intervals whose derivative is zero where defined off the Cantor set yet whose total rise is one.
major_error_concepts: Concluding zero derivative almost everywhere implies constant without the right hypotheses and measure theory.

cards.prompt: Define Cantor-set construction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The nested closed-set construction deleting middle thirds with compactness uncountability empty interior and zero-length-cover properties separated.
required_concepts: The nested closed-set construction deleting middle thirds with compactness uncountability empty interior and zero-length-cover properties separated.
major_error_concepts: Calling it countable because it has no intervals.

cards.prompt: Define a Banach contraction and distinguish a uniform contraction factor from merely pairwise strict shortening.
cards.definition: A contraction on a metric space (X,d) is a self-map T:X→X for which one constant q with 0≤q<1 satisfies d(Tx,Ty)≤q d(x,y) for every x,y in X. A separate factor for each pair, or merely strict shortening without a uniform q<1, is not the Banach-contraction hypothesis.
required_concepts: T maps the space into itself.
One common q in [0,1) works for every pair.
Point-dependent shortening factors need not give a contraction.
major_error_concepts: Any self-map that brings each distinct pair strictly closer is a Banach contraction, even when no common q<1 works.

cards.term: Fixed-point formulation of an initial-value problem
cards.prompt: Define Fixed-point formulation of an initial-value problem. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The controlled reformulation of an initial-value problem as an integral fixed-point equation on a complete function space under a local contraction bound.
required_concepts: The controlled reformulation of an initial-value problem as an integral fixed-point equation on a complete function space under a local contraction bound.
major_error_concepts: Calling the illustrative proof a full ODE existence theory.

cards.prompt: Define Jordan decomposition for bounded variation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The theorem that a real bounded-variation function is a difference of two increasing functions with normalization and uniqueness qualifications.
required_concepts: The theorem that a real bounded-variation function is a difference of two increasing functions with normalization and uniqueness qualifications.
major_error_concepts: Confusing this with Jordan canonical form or measure decomposition.

cards.prompt: Define Nowhere-differentiable continuous function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A continuous function lacking a finite derivative at every point and demonstrating that continuity gives no generic smoothness.
required_concepts: A continuous function lacking a finite derivative at every point and demonstrating that continuity gives no generic smoothness.
major_error_concepts: Assuming a jagged plot is proof of nowhere differentiability.

cards.prompt: State the a priori and a posteriori error bounds for Picard iteration under a verified contraction factor.
cards.definition: Under the Banach fixed-point hypotheses, set x_(n+1)=T(x_n) and let 0≤q<1 be a verified global contraction factor. For n≥1, d(x_n,x*)≤q^n d(x_1,x_0)/(1-q) is an a priori bound, while d(x_n,x*)≤q d(x_n,x_(n-1))/(1-q) is an a posteriori bound. A factor estimated from a few observed iterate ratios is not automatically a valid global q.
required_concepts: State the indexed a priori bound q^n d(x_1,x_0)/(1-q).
State the a posteriori bound q d(x_n,x_(n-1))/(1-q).
The contraction factor is a proved uniform bound, not just an observed ratio.
major_error_concepts: The distance to the fixed point is always at most the latest step size, independently of q.

cards.prompt: Define Qualified Real Analysis I conclusion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The narrow statement supported by exact hypotheses proofs counterexamples and reviews with numerical empirical learner and downstream claims denied.
required_concepts: The narrow statement supported by exact hypotheses proofs counterexamples and reviews with numerical empirical learner and downstream claims denied.
major_error_concepts: Calling course artifact completion proof of research-level analysis mastery.

cards.prompt: Define quantifier-order distinction.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The explicit comparison of pointwise versus uniform Cauchy versus convergent local versus global and for-every/there-exists arrangements.
required_concepts: The explicit comparison of pointwise versus uniform Cauchy versus convergent local versus global and for-every/there-exists arrangements.
major_error_concepts: Swapping words without reversing all quantifiers.

cards.prompt: Define Riemann-Stieltjes integral. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The limit or Darboux-style integral of f against increments of a monotone or bounded-variation integrator alpha with both roles distinguished.
required_concepts: The limit or Darboux-style integral of f against increments of a monotone or bounded-variation integrator alpha with both roles distinguished.
major_error_concepts: Replacing d alpha with alpha'(x)dx when the derivative does not represent all variation.

cards.prompt: Define Stieltjes integration by parts. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The identity integral f d alpha plus integral alpha d f equals endpoint product difference under conditions guaranteeing both integrals.
required_concepts: The identity integral f d alpha plus integral alpha d f equals endpoint product difference under conditions guaranteeing both integrals.
major_error_concepts: Using the identity before proving both Stieltjes integrals exist.

cards.prompt: Define Total variation of a function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The supremum over partitions of sums of absolute increments with bounded variation meaning finite total variation.
required_concepts: The supremum over partitions of sums of absolute increments with bounded variation meaning finite total variation.
major_error_concepts: Using one partition sum as the total variation.
